plan: OpenVibe.Surf: one room with three surfs. Ride is CS-style surf in the browser served by OpenVibe.Games; Watch is lean-back channel surfing over OpenVibe.Live's live streams, clips and AI moments; Web is Surf with Vibe, where an agent browses for you on a private desk through OpenVibe.Actor.
runtime: node 22, express 4, openvibe-shared/shell; stateless (no database, no Valkey, no Events)
summary: The service skeleton for openvibe.surf: Network sign-in as OAuth client `surf` (PKCE S256, httpOnly surf_at/surf_rt cookies), the Watch feed merged from OpenVibe.Live (live streams by viewers, then clips and moments interleaved by freshness, no same-channel runs, cached 30 s, each source given 2 s, failures named in `sources`), the Ride proxy to OpenVibe.Games' /api/surf/maps (cached 60 s, games: 'not_ready' while Games' new routes answer 404, an embed URL per map), and Surf with Vibe: a signed-in, same-origin POST that creates one OpenVibe.Actor task with the person's own Network token as a Bearer, an Idempotency-Key and a cited browsing brief, plus /web/go as the no-JavaScript form. The pages are placeholders for the main session: stable sf- ids and classes, semantic HTML, readable without JavaScript.
works: Sign-in with OpenVibe.Network: OAuth 2 authorization code, PKCE S256, state check, server-side exchange, httpOnly surf_at/surf_rt cookies, sanitizeNext (own origins only, no control characters or backslashes)

Watch GET /api/v1/watch/feed?topic=all|live|clips|moments&cursor=: merges OpenVibe.Live's /api/streams, /api/content/feed?type=clips and /api/content/moments?type=clips into one item shape, ranks live by viewers then moments/clips by freshness with no channel twice in a row, caches 30 s, 2 s per source, a failing source left out and named in sources, public max-age=30

Ride GET /api/v1/ride/maps and /api/v1/ride/maps/:id: proxies OpenVibe.Games' /api/surf/maps routes, adds each map's embed_url (https://openvibe.games/play/surf?map=<id>&embed=1), caches 60 s, Games 404 → empty list/map shell with games: 'not_ready'

Web POST /api/v1/web/tasks: signed in, same-origin, query 3–500 characters, sends the person's surf_at token to OpenVibe.Actor as a Bearer with an Idempotency-Key and the prefixed browsing brief, answers { task_id, page }, and passes Actor's 4xx refusal through in words
GET /web/go?q=: the same task as a plain form for no-JavaScript: 303 to the Actor task page, sign-in redirect for a guest, Actor's refusal in plain words

Server-rendered pages: / (three tiles), /ride (maps list and first embed), /ride/:map (name, tier, stages, records, embed), /watch (feed list with thumbnails and play links, HLS hooks for the main session's video), /web (the form), /developers and a 404; public max-age=60 with Vary: Cookie, signed-in private, no-store

Crawl artifacts (robots.txt, sitemap.xml with the public pages and Ride maps, llms.txt), /api/health, /api/ready (degraded when Network/Live/Games/Actor do not answer), /release.json, /release-metrics, /shared/*
Helmet with the network's CSP (Games and Live frames, openvibe.media HLS), per-IP 120/min on /api and /auth, content-hashed /css and /js, graceful stop
Deploy files: openvibe-surf.service, nginx vhost for openvibe.surf on 127.0.0.1:5110 with the forms zone, /auth/me on the API zone and /internal + /metrics 404

Tests: feed merge/order/shape/failing source/30 s cache/cursor, ride proxy/cache/not_ready/failure, web 401/403/Actor Bearer + Idempotency-Key + prefixed text/refusal/redirect, SSO (Design's cases), pages/cache headers/CSP, discovery
notYet: The pages' design and public/css/surf.css + public/js/surf.js: the main session writes them; today the views are semantic placeholders and the assets are one-comment files (the HLS <video> player is the main session's script)
OpenVibe.Games' GET /api/surf/maps and /api/surf/maps/:id are being added in parallel; until they ship, Ride answers games: 'not_ready'
A Surf service manifest and capabilities in OpenVibe.Contracts: this service has no capability of its own and no other service calls it
Deployment: the deploy files are written, but the service is not deployed yet
